clue.text: See 26 across
Stretch half of duck portion

indicators.note: half of the four-letter word duck means only its first two letters are used

parts.note: a portion or allotted share is a ration

explanation.surface: Someone stretches a half-share of a duck dinner to last longer.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretch is a period of time, as in a long stretch in prison, which is a length of time.

clue.text: Achilles, perhaps, plucking tail from waterbird

indicators.note: plucking the tail from a word removes its last letter, here the final N

parts.note: a heron is a long-legged wading waterbird

explanation.surface: The Greek warrior Achilles is pictured plucking the tail feathers off a waterbird.
explanation.definitionFit: Achilles is an example of a legendary Greek champion of the Trojan War, a warrior of myth.

clue.text: First-rate or second-rate clue, the first to be last in

parts.note: second-rate things are B-grade, B being the second class after A

indicators.note: the first letter of the word clue is moved to its end, giving LUEC

parts.note: something in or fashionable is hip

explanation.surface: A puzzle remark asking whether a clue is first-rate or second-rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is a link here. 'the first to be last' moves the C of clue to the back: LUEC.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue-chip stock is the most reliable on the market, so the term means top-quality or first-class.

clue.text: Old and comical duck

indicators.note: comical suggests the letters of 'Old and' are played about with, clownishly rearranged

explanation.surface: An elderly and funny duck is described.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface itself describes the cartoon duck, old and comical.
explanation.definitionFit: Donald is the famous Disney cartoon duck, so the name stands for one particular duck.

clue.text: Apparent Opposition leader well-advised to take time

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of Opposition
to take means to receive inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: a well-advised course of action is a sensible one

explanation.surface: It seems the leader of the Opposition would be wise to take his time.
explanation.walkthrough: SENSIBLE takes T after its first letter: STENSIBLE, with O in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostensible means seeming or professed on the surface, so it is a synonym of apparent.

clue.text: Other half of duck, covering top of pancake

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: to duck someone is to plunge them in water, to souse them

indicators.note: top of in a down clue means the first letter of pancake

explanation.surface: Someone eats the other half of a duck with a pancake on top, as in Peking duck.
explanation.definitionFit: Other half is a jocular idiom for one's partner in marriage, husband or wife.

clue.text: Very much like duck

definitions.meaning: to be very fond of something, adore it
a score of nil, as zero in tennis is called

explanation.surface: Someone who looks very much like a duck.
explanation.definitionFit: Love means great fondness; in tennis it is a score of zero, as a duck is in cricket.

clue.text: Morning milk, please

parts.note: AM is the abbreviation for morning, ante meridiem
to milk something is to exploit it, to use it

explanation.surface: A polite request for morning milk.
explanation.definitionFit: To please someone is to entertain or delight them, which is a synonym of the answer's verb.

clue.text: Appearance by Potus, deranged in respects

parts.note: a look is a person's appearance

indicators.note: deranged means disordered, so the letters of Potus are rearranged

explanation.surface: An appearance by the US President, who is called deranged in some respects.
explanation.walkthrough: POTUS, President of the United States, is rearranged to SUPTO. 'by' and 'in' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To look up to someone is an idiom for admiring them, holding them in respect.

clue.text: Drama to escalate about head of church and end of dogma

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word goes around the second

parts.note: to escalate is to rise rapidly, to soar
the Pope is head of the Roman Catholic Church

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of dogma

explanation.surface: A dramatic escalation surrounding the head of the church and the end of a doctrine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of church' looks like a first-letter pick for C, but it is the Pope himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A soap opera is a type of serialised television drama, originally sponsored by soap makers.

clue.text: Oddie's last report of blue duck

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of the word Oddie's, ignoring the apostrophe
report here means a spoken account, so the word is given as it is heard

parts.note: blue jokes are lewd ones

explanation.surface: The birdwatcher Bill Oddie's final report of sighting a blue duck.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill Oddie is a British TV birdwatcher, which suits the bird surface. Oddie's last letter is E, ignoring the apostrophe-S.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck something is to dodge or evade it, which is a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Head of snow goose eating a leafy plant

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of snow
eating means taking in, so one word swallows the other

parts.note: to goose someone is to pinch their bottom

explanation.surface: A snow goose feeding on a leafy plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinach is a green vegetable grown for its edible leaves.

clue.text: Opinions in Khan's letters ignored in treatment of skinheads

indicators.note: ignored means the named letters are left out of the mix
treatment means working on, so the letters of skinheads are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of the name Khan

explanation.surface: Views held in Khan's correspondence were disregarded when dealing with skinheads.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove K, H, A, N from SKINHEADS and rearrange what is left, SIEDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sides are positions or viewpoints in an argument, so they stand for opinions taken.

clue.text: Tho' Marconi designed the first modern time machine, this …

definitions.text: the first modern time machine, this

indicators.note: designed means put together in a new pattern, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Although Marconi created it, the first modern time machine is this one, continuing into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs the sentence into 16 down; the radio pioneer Marconi is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: The Atomichron of 1956 was the first commercial atomic clock, a device that keeps time precisely.

clue.text: Perhaps split, braided to left

indicators.note: to left means read leftwards, from the end back to the start

parts.note: braided hair is tressed

explanation.surface: Hair perhaps split and braided over to the left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'split' suggests hair or a division, but it is a banana split.
explanation.definitionFit: A banana split is an example of a sweet course served after the main meal.

clue.text: … carries leaders of the original Tory establishment still

indicators.note: leaders of the following words are their initial letters

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: it carries the leaders of the original Tory establishment still.
explanation.definitionFit: To tote is an informal verb for carrying or hauling something about.

clue.text: Dog found in goose cages

indicators.note: the phrase cages the answer, holding it inside its letters

explanation.surface: A dog discovered inside some goose cages.
explanation.definitionFit: The dingo is a wild dog native to Australia.

clue.text: An Englishman in Australia in May gets a duck, going in

indicators.note: going in means the second piece is placed inside the first

parts.note: Theresa May was PM, the Prime Minister, when the puzzle appeared
a duck is a nil score, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: An English visitor to Australia in May is served a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' looks like the month but is Theresa May, then Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Pom is Australian slang for a British, especially English, person.

clue.text: This duck seen in damn rain, swimming

indicators.note: swimming suggests moving about freely, so the letters of damn rain are rearranged

explanation.surface: This duck was spotted paddling in heavy rain.
explanation.definitionFit: The mandarin is a brightly coloured species of Asian duck.

clue.text: Goose found in London, perhaps getting angry

definitions.meaning: a small dark goose species of northern coasts

definitions.text: found in London, perhaps getting angry
definitions.meaning: a place in London when it gets cross

explanation.surface: A goose seen in London, maybe turning aggressive.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is cryptic: add 'cross' (angry) to the answer and you get Brent Cross, a well-known area of north London.
explanation.definitionFit: The brent is a species of small dark goose; Brent is also a London borough with a Cross.

clue.text: Stirs up core of patently wrong uprising over Poles

indicators.note: core of picks the central letters of patently
uprising in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: wrong as a noun is wickedness, evil
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: An obviously misguided uprising over Poland stirs things up.
explanation.walkthrough: Patently has eight letters, so its core is EN. 'over' is a link: in a down clue the pieces sit above one another.
explanation.definitionFit: To enliven something is to make it livelier, to animate or stir it up.

clue.text: Dismissal for duck, perhaps

definitions.meaning: duck is a strong cotton cloth

explanation.surface: Getting fired because of a duck, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' is not the bird but a heavy fabric, like canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sacked is dismissal; sacking is also coarse woven fabric, of which duck is an example.

clue.text: Duck down feather: it's ultimate stuffing for sofa

indicators.note: stuffing for means filling, so the letter goes inside the word for sofa

parts.note: a couch is a sofa

indicators.note: it's ultimate, read as its ultimate, picks the last letter of feather

explanation.surface: A duck down feather is the final filling for a sofa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck down' looks like the filling material, but it is the verb phrase. 'it's' is read as 'its'.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck down is to bend low to avoid being seen or hit, which is to stoop.

clue.text: Leave mostly stupid, horrific

parts.note: to leave is to go

indicators.note: mostly means almost all of the word, dropping its last letter

parts.note: a stupid person is thick

explanation.surface: A leave of absence that was mostly stupid and horrific.
explanation.definitionFit: Gothic fiction is a genre of horror and the macabre, so the word can mean horrific.

clue.text: Pointless pointless pointers

indicators.note: pointless here means losing a compass point, the letter S

parts.note: pointless means unnecessary, needless

explanation.surface: A mock-insult: pointless, utterly pointless pointers.
explanation.walkthrough: The same word does two jobs: first as a synonym, then as the instruction to remove S, a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Needles are pointers, as on a compass or dial gauge.

clue.text: Goose detects sounds, though one just won't listen

parts.note: a goose is a silly person, a fool, as is a clot
to detect sounds is to hear, so 'detects sounds' gives hears

explanation.surface: A goose picks up noises, though some people never pay attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goose' looks like the bird of the puzzle's duck-and-goose theme, but here it is a fool. 'though' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A British informal insult for someone who is inattentive or deaf to what is said, as if their hearing were muffled by fabric.

clue.text: Temporary home for cheeky kids without boundaries

indicators.note: without boundaries means losing the outer letters at each end

parts.note: mischievous children are scamps

explanation.surface: A holiday base for cheeky children allowed to run riot.
explanation.definitionFit: A camp is a place of tents or huts offering short-term lodging.

clue.text: Duck next to edge of roof, the result of having a drink?

definitions.text: the result of having a drink?

parts.note: the teal is a small freshwater duck
the eaves are the overhanging lower edge of a roof

explanation.surface: A duck sitting beside the roof's edge, which may come from having a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'next to' is a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: What remains in the cup after drinking a brew made without a bag: the residue of a cuppa.

clue.text: Mirror leaders excoriating Commons: "Useless chamber"

indicators.note: leaders are first letters of the two words that follow
Useless is read as use-less: the letters U, S, E are removed

parts.note: a chamber of parliament is a house, such as the House of Commons

explanation.surface: A newspaper, the Mirror, with leading articles berating the Commons as a useless chamber.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mirror is a British tabloid newspaper, and 'leaders' suggests editorials. 'Useless' splits into USE-less.
explanation.definitionFit: To echo is to repeat or reflect back, as a mirror reflects.

clue.text: It's said to be easy, following duck in this way, scoring more

definitions.text: It's said to be easy, following duck

parts.note: so means thus, in this manner
a side scoring more than its rival is up

explanation.surface: Following a duck, scoring more is said to come easily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' suggests a cricket nought, but duck soup is American slang for an easy task.
explanation.definitionFit: Duck soup is an American idiom for something simple to do, so the word after duck completes it.

clue.text: Extremely small painter, cubist initially, absorbed in Boatman's reflection

indicators.note: absorbed means taken in, so the letter goes inside the painter's name

parts.note: Joan Miro was a Spanish surrealist painter

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of cubist
a reflection shows things backwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: Boatman is the setter, so Boatman's is I'M, I am

explanation.surface: A tiny painter, a cubist at first, is lost in the setter's thoughts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflection' reverses IN + I'M, giving MINI.
explanation.definitionFit: Micro and mini both mean very small, so the doubled term is an intensified word for tiny.

clue.text: One who has faith in house God destroyed, sacrificing goose

indicators.note: destroyed means broken up, so the letters are rearranged
sacrificing means giving up, so those letters are taken out of the mix

explanation.surface: A believer finds his household god wrecked, after sacrificing a goose.
explanation.walkthrough: From the letters of IN HOUSE GOD remove those of GOOSE, leaving INHUD to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of the major Indian religion is a believer, a person of faith.
